text.p: The Dakar-Agades-Dakar rally claimed its 34th fatality on Sunday when French motorcyclist Jean-Pierre Leduc was killed in a crash halfway through the second stage in Mali.
Leduc, 45, fell from his KTM bike after 247 km in the 505-km stage from Toumbacounda to Kayes.
"Doctors reached him 20 minutes after the fall but nothing could be done," a spokeswoman for the organisers said.
She said Leduc, who was married with a child, apparently fell while riding alone. Doctors rushed to the site of the accident after another competitor found him and sent a distress call.
Since its launch in 1979, the race has been notoriously dangerous.
Riders, drivers and spectators have been killed on the trails of north-western Africa, including the event's creator, Frenchman Thierry Sabine, who died in a helicopter crash in 1986.
The second stage, which took the competitors from Senegal to Mali, was won by French driver Jean-Louis Schlesser, who ousted compatriot Jean-Pierre Fontenay at the top of the overall standings.
Schlesser, in a Buggy, now leads three Mitsubishis but he failed to open a decisive gap on roads made treacherous by dust.
France's Bruno Saby lies second overall, 48 seconds behind Schlesser, with Japan's Kenjiro Shinozuka third and Fontenay, who had two punctures, fourth.
In the motorcycle section, four-times winner Stephane Peterhansel had another easy win while most of his rivals lost precious time in falls.
